title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 158 (Repayment, by bailor, of necessary expenses)

content.overview: Section 158 provides that where, by the conditions of the bailment, the goods are to be kept or to be carried, or to have work done upon them by the bailee for the bailor, and the bailee is to receive no remuneration, the bailor shall repay to the bailee the necessary expenses incurred by him for the purpose of the bailment.
content.glance: In a gratuitous bailment where the bailee keeps, carries or works on the goods without remuneration, the bailor must repay the necessary expenses incurred for the purpose of the bailment.
content.study: Where, by the conditions of the bailment, the goods are to be kept or to be carried, or to have work done upon them by the bailee for the bailor, and the bailee is to receive no remuneration, the bailor shall repay to the bailee the necessary expenses incurred by him for the purpose of the bailment. Current-law framing: applies to gratuitous bailments; expenses must be necessary for the purpose.

enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 158 requires the bailor to repay necessary expenses incurred by the bailee where the bailment is gratuitous and the goods are to be kept, carried or have work done upon them. It protects the unpaid bailee from bearing necessary costs.
examples: Necessary storage or upkeep costs in a free bailment must be repaid by the bailor.
distinctions: Applies only where no remuneration is to be received; remunerated bailments are governed by the contract.
